audit.why: 51.57% over 1588 games with the chart giving Rumble 2/3/6 and Yasuo the two-item stage. The text already frames it as a lane Rumble bullies early and must not extend into — that matches both the data and the kits (Flamespitter is not a projectile, so Wind Wall never protects him from the core damage).

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 2-3 and Level 4-5 spikes reference Wind Wall and Sweeping Blade with no cooldowns, so neither reads as a spike you can play around.
audit.why: Wind Wall is 25/23/21/19/17 seconds. At rank 1 a baited Wind Wall gives Rumble roughly twenty seconds where every Electro-Harpoon connects — that is the actual level-2-3 spike and it is currently unstated.
audit.corrected: Attach Wind Wall's 25s rank-1 cooldown to the early spike and Last Breath's 70s rank-1 cooldown to the level 6 discussion.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most exploitable rule in Yasuo's kit is absent everywhere: Sweeping Blade cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds. The text repeatedly says he 'dashes repeatedly' and 'chains dashes' without noting that he can only do that through separate units. Against a Rumble standing away from the wave, Yasuo gets one dash in and no dash out.
audit.why: Riot's own Sweeping Blade text: 'Cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds.' Combined with Flamespitter being a 3-second cone that only needs him to stay in front of you, this turns his engage into a commitment rather than a poke. It also makes the existing 'freeze near your side' advice mechanically justified instead of vibes.
audit.corrected: State the no-recast rule and connect it to wave position: minion-free ground between you means his dash is one-way.

audit.whatIsWrong: The late-game section calls Yasuo's passive 'Double Critical Strike'. That is not the name of the ability. Yasuo's passive is Way of the Wanderer.
audit.why: Riot Data Dragon lists P as Way of the Wanderer: increased critical strike chance plus a shield that builds while moving and triggers on champion or monster damage. 'Double Critical Strike' is a fabricated name of exactly the class the calibration examples warn about.
audit.corrected: Use Way of the Wanderer, and mention the flow shield, which is the part that actually matters against Rumble's chip.

edits.before: Your Q-into-double-E combo comes online and Yasuo cannot block Flamespitter with Wind Wall — start dictating trade windows.
edits.after: Q into double-E is online and Wind Wall cannot block the Flamespitter cone — the Wall is 25s at rank 1, so bait it with a harpoon.

edits.before: Yasuo's Sweeping Blade stacks let him dash repeatedly through minions to close distance — manage Heat so you can W-shield his EQ and punish.
edits.after: Sweeping Blade cannot re-target the same enemy for a few seconds — pull him off the wave and he gets one dash in and none back out.

edits.before: All three basics online: lead with first E to slow his Sweeping Blade approach, W-shield his knockup, then unload second E and Danger Zone Q — his gap-close becomes your punish.
edits.after: Lead with the first Harpoon, W-shield the Steel Tempest knockup, then unload the second — Sweeping Blade cannot re-target you for seconds, so his dash strands him inside your Danger Zone cone.

edits.before: At Level 1 you are solid but not yet in control — Yasuo can dash through minions with Sweeping Blade to keep his distance and avoid eating a full Flamespitter cone. The key interaction to know immediately: his W Wind Wall cannot block your Q Flamespitter because it is a cone, not a projectile. Your E Electro-Harpoon IS a projectile and he will Wind Wall it if he sees it coming, so bait the Wall down before you throw E or use it to interrupt his dash approach. At Level 2 you get your first real window: EQ-slow him into a Danger Zone Flamespitter and he has no answer that does not cost him significant health. By Level 3 with both E charges available, lead with the first harpoon to slow his dash cycle, force him to commit his Steel Tempest stack into your W shield, and then walk him down with the second harpoon while your Q deals sustained Danger Zone damage.
edits.after: At Level 1 you are solid but not yet in control — Yasuo can dash through minions with Sweeping Blade to keep his distance and avoid eating a full Flamespitter cone. At Level 2 you get your first real window: EQ-slow him into a Danger Zone Flamespitter and he has no answer that does not cost him significant health. By Level 3 with both E charges available, lead with the first harpoon to slow his dash cycle, force him to commit his Steel Tempest stack into your W shield, and then walk him down with the second harpoon while your Q deals sustained Danger Zone damage.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 become a chess match around Yasuo's Sweeping Blade stacks and your Heat bar. He will try to use minions to chain dashes and shorten the time he spends inside your Flamespitter cone — freeze the wave near your side of the lane so he must dash through open space toward you rather than threading minions. Keep your Heat in the Danger Zone before he engages so your W shield is empowered when his EQ knockup lands. At Level 6 the dynamic shifts in your favor in a different dimension: your Equalizer does not need to be a direct hit to win the exchange. Drop it along the path he wants to dash through after a Steel Tempest stack, and the slow plus sustained damage makes his entire EQ sequence risky. He cannot Wind Wall the Equalizer rockets. His Last Breath at 6 requires a knockup he generates himself — respect the EQ combo but do not let it keep you out of trading range entirely.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 become a chess match around Yasuo's Sweeping Blade and your Heat bar. He chains dashes through minions to shorten his time inside the Flamespitter cone — freeze the wave near your side so he must cross open space, and remember Sweeping Blade cannot re-target the same enemy for a few seconds: with no minions between you he gets one dash in and none back out. Keep your Heat in the Danger Zone before he engages so your W shield is empowered when the Steel Tempest knockup lands. At Level 6 your Equalizer does not need to be a direct hit to win the exchange. Drop it along the path he wants to dash through after a Steel Tempest stack, and the slow plus sustained damage makes his entire sequence risky. He cannot Wind Wall the Equalizer rockets. Last Breath is 70 seconds at rank 1 and needs a knockup he generates himself — respect the combo without letting it price you out of trading range.

edits.before: Full-crit Yasuo with Infinity Edge and Navori Quickblades hits hard enough to blow through your Scrap Shield in a single trade rotation, and his E mobility makes it genuinely difficult to land Electro-Harpoon on a moving target. Play your Equalizer as a zoning tool in teamfights rather than trying to solo him — a well-placed rocket line across a chokepoint negates his dash angles entirely and makes him irrelevant for the five seconds it burns. If you are ahead from lane you can still win short trades by entering Danger Zone first and walking at him, but do not extend a brawl past your first Flamespitter rotation. His passive Double Critical Strike and Last Breath make extended fights his domain at two items.

notes: All four packet suspectNames here are FALSE POSITIVES — 'Land Equalizer', 'Use Last Breath', 'His Last Breath' and 'Wind Walled' are the real Riot names (or ordinary inflections of them), so I changed none of them. UNVERIFIED and deliberately left alone: the existing claim 'He cannot Wind Wall the Equalizer rockets' (in mid) and 'Equalizer cannot be Wind Walled' (whys[4]). Rumble's kit file flags The Equalizer as a projectile and Wind Wall's description says it blocks all enemy projectiles, so the file, read literally, contradicts the page. Riot's R text ('fires off a group of rockets, creating a wall of flames') is ambiguous about whether the flame zone is the projectile, and I could not settle it from local data — the brief says leave it and report it, which is what I did. Also note Rumble's Scrap Shield carries bogus 'knockup' and 'terrain' derived flags; I wrote nothing that has Scrap Shield blocking Sweeping Blade.
